area: default.json packageRules (automerge minor/patch/digest + github-actions digest re-enable)
body:
## Problem

`default.json:89-97` sets `{"automerge": true, "automergeType": "branch", "matchUpdateTypes": ["minor","patch","digest"]}`,
and `default.json:236-253` re-enables `digest` updates for the whole `github-actions` manager.
No later rule narrows `automerge`/`automergeType` for that combination, so **every** GitHub Action
digest update is auto-merged straight onto the base branch with no pull request.

The top-level `minimumReleaseAge: "3 days"` (`default.json:77`) does not apply to digest updates:
digest updates are pushed directly onto the update list and never pass through the release-age filter.

## Evidence

Renovate `lib/workers/repository/process/lookup/index.ts:647-654`:
```ts
if (config.currentDigest) {
  if (!config.digestOneAndOnly || !res.updates.length) {
    // digest update
    res.updates.push({
      updateType: 'digest',
      newValue: config.currentValue,
    });
  }
}
```
This push happens outside `filterInternalChecks()` (`lookup/filter-checks.ts`), which only iterates
`sortedReleases` — i.e. version updates. A digest-only update therefore never reaches
`checkMinimumReleaseAge()` and is never held.

`automergeType: "branch"` additionally means no PR is opened at all, so there is no artifact to review
and no review requirement to satisfy.

## Impact

Failing scenario: an attacker compromises a third-party action's repo and force-moves the floating tag
`v4` to a malicious commit (the tj-actions/changed-files pattern). Renovate's next run sees a new digest
for that tag, creates the branch, and — with no cooldown and no PR — merges the new SHA into the default
branch of every repo consuming this preset. `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` exists precisely to stop a
moved tag from silently changing what runs in CI; automerging its digest updates hands that protection back.

## Fix

Exclude `digest` from unattended branch automerge for third-party actions. In `default.json`, drop
`"digest"` from the minor/patch automerge rule at lines 89-97:

```json
{ "automerge": true, "automergeType": "branch", "matchUpdateTypes": ["minor", "patch"] }
```

and, if action digests should still be automerged for trusted sources only, add that back on the
`@ivuorinen actions` rule (which already scopes to `ivuorinen/actions*`). Third-party action digests
then raise a normal PR for review.

## Resolution
Dropped 'digest' from the minor/patch branch-automerge rule in default.json. Third-party action digests now raise a reviewable PR; only ivuorinen/actions digests automerge, inheriting automerge from the trusted-source rule now last in packageRules. Added a description block on both rules recording why. README gained a 'Digest updates and automerge' section.
title: GitHub Action digest updates automerge to the default branch with no PR, no review and no cooldown

body:
## Problem

There is no `.github/workflows/` directory and no `ci:` block in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
(no pre-commit.ci integration). The three validators (`renovate-config-validator --strict` x2 and
`check-renovate-preset`) only ever run if a contributor has installed the git hooks locally and does
not use `--no-verify`.

Meanwhile `README.md:10-17` instructs consumers to use `"extends": ["github>ivuorinen/renovate-config"]`,
which resolves the **default branch HEAD** on every Renovate run — no tag, no pin.

## Evidence

```
$ git ls-files
.editorconfig
.github/renovate.json          <- only file under .github/
.gitignore
.pre-commit-config.yaml
CLAUDE.md
LICENSE
README.md
default.json
$ grep -n 'ci:' .pre-commit-config.yaml
(no match)
```
Nothing in the repository executes the validators in response to a push or a pull request.

## Impact

Failing scenario: a commit lands on `main` with a malformed `packageRules` entry or an invalid regex.
Every repository extending `github>ivuorinen/renovate-config` picks it up on its next Renovate run and
raises a config-error issue or stops updating dependencies entirely. The blast radius is every
ivuorinen repo at once, and the defect is only discovered from the downstream failures.

This is the same class of gap that let the three custom-manager regex defects in this audit ship
(see the `versioningTemplate`, Dockerfile `ENV` and Makefile comment findings).

## Fix

Add `.github/workflows/validate.yml` running the same hooks CI-side:

```yaml
name: validate
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  pre-commit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha>  # pin per helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests
      - uses: actions/setup-python@<sha>
      - uses: pre-commit/action@<sha>
```

and make it a required status check on `main`. Alternatively enable pre-commit.ci by adding a `ci:`
block to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.

## Resolution
Added .github/workflows/validate.yml running the full pre-commit suite on push to main and on every pull_request, with contents:read permissions and both actions SHA-pinned per the preset's own helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests policy (actions/checkout v7.0.1, actions/setup-python v7.0.0). README and CLAUDE.md now state why local hooks are insufficient. Make it a required status check on main to close the loop.
title: No CI gate: default.json is consumed live off the default branch but nothing validates it on push or PR

body:
## Problem

Commit `10a624a` added a top-level `minimumReleaseAge: "3 days"` (`default.json:77`), widening the hold
from npm-only (`security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm`) to **every** datasource. `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour` is
left unset, and its default is `timestamp-required`: an update whose release carries no `releaseTimestamp`
is marked pending rather than allowed through. With the default `internalChecksFilter: "strict"` that
pending state suppresses the branch, and it never clears because the timestamp will never appear.

`default.json:61-63` deliberately enables the `git-submodules` manager, whose datasource is `git-refs` —
git ref listings carry no release timestamps.

## Evidence

Renovate `lib/workers/repository/process/lookup/filter-checks.ts`:
```ts
export function checkMinimumReleaseAge(config, releaseTimestamp) {
  ...
  if (releaseTimestamp) {
    return { isPending: getElapsedMs(releaseTimestamp) < minimumReleaseAgeMs, ... };
  }
  return {
    isPending: config.minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour === 'timestamp-required',   // <- no timestamp => pending
    minimumReleaseAgeMs,
    hasTimestamp: false,
  };
}
```
Defaults, `lib/config/options/index.ts`:
```
2148:    name: 'minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour',
2152:    default: 'timestamp-required',
2188:    name: 'internalChecksFilter',
2192:    default: 'strict',
```
And in the same file, when every candidate is pending:
```ts
release = pendingReleases.pop();
if (internalChecksFilter === 'strict') { pendingChecks = true; }
```
Renovate logs this as: *"Marking N release(s) as pending, as they do not have a releaseTimestamp and
we're running with minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-required"*.

`lib/modules/manager/git-submodules/index.ts` confirms the datasource:
```ts
export const supportedDatasources = [GitRefsDatasource.id];
```

## Impact

Failing scenario: a repo consuming this preset has a git submodule. Before `10a624a` it received submodule
update PRs. After it, every submodule update is permanently "pending" on the dependency dashboard and no
branch is ever created — the manager the preset explicitly turns on is silently inert. The same applies to
any custom-regex dependency whose datasource returns no timestamp. Nothing errors; updates just stop.

## Fix

Either relax the behaviour globally in `default.json`:

```json
"minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour": "timestamp-optional",
```

(updates without a timestamp proceed, with a warning logged), or keep `timestamp-required` and scope the
hold to datasources that supply timestamps by exempting the timestamp-less ones:

```json
{ "matchManagers": ["git-submodules"], "minimumReleaseAge": null }
```

## Resolution
Added a packageRule exempting matchManagers:[git-submodules] from minimumReleaseAge. Kept the fail-closed timestamp-required default for every other datasource rather than globally relaxing to timestamp-optional, so the 3-day hold still applies wherever a releaseTimestamp exists. Documented in the README 'Other configuration' table.
title: Global minimumReleaseAge freezes every dependency whose datasource returns no releaseTimestamp, including git-submodules

body:
## Problem

The match string at `default.json:20` starts `ENV [A-Z]+_VERSION=`. `[A-Z]+` cannot match `_` or a digit,
and the literal `ENV ` anchors the match, so the variable name must be a single uppercase run immediately
followed by `_VERSION`. Any multi-word name (`DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION`, `NODE_EXPORTER_VERSION`) or a name
containing a digit (`PHP8_VERSION`) fails to match and the dependency is never tracked — with no error.

## Evidence

```js
const re = /ENV [A-Z]+_VERSION=(?<currentValue>.*) # (?<datasource>.*?)\/(?<depName>.*?)(\&versioning=(?<versioning>.*?))?\s/;
```
```
MATCH    "ENV HELM_VERSION=3.14.0 # github-releases/helm/helm" -> depName=helm/helm
NO MATCH "ENV DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=2.24.0 # github-releases/docker/compose"
NO MATCH "ENV NODE_EXPORTER_VERSION=1.7.0 # github-releases/prometheus/node_exporter"
NO MATCH "ENV PHP8_VERSION=8.3.0 # github-releases/php/php-src"
NO MATCH "ARG HELM_VERSION=3.14.0 # github-releases/helm/helm"
```

## Impact

A consuming repo annotates `ENV DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=2.24.0 # github-releases/docker/compose` exactly as
`README.md:66-69` documents, and Renovate never raises an update for it. The dependency silently rots; there
is no config error, no dashboard entry, and no log line pointing at the cause. Multi-word tool names are the
common case, so this misses more Dockerfiles than it catches.

## Fix

Widen the variable-name class in `default.json:20`:

```
ENV [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_VERSION=(?<currentValue>.*) # (?<datasource>.*?)/(?<depName>.*?)(\&versioning=(?<versioning>.*?))?\s
```

If `ARG` should also be covered, make the keyword alternation explicit: `(?:ENV|ARG) `.
Update the pattern quoted in `README.md:74` to match.

## Resolution
Widened the variable-name class to [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_VERSION. Verified against test/fixtures/Dockerfile: DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION, NODE_EXPORTER_VERSION and PHP8_VERSION now extract, and the &versioning= override still captures. ARG deliberately still not matched (documented). README pattern block updated.
title: Dockerfile ENV manager silently skips every version variable whose name has more than one word or a digit

body:
## Problem

The match string at `default.json:35` requires the captured `depName` to be followed immediately by a
newline: `depName=(?<depName>\S+)\n`. Renovate's own documented convention for regex-manager comments puts
optional fields after `depName` — `versioning=`, `extractVersion=`, `registryUrl=`. `\S+` cannot consume the
intervening space, so backtracking cannot rescue the match and the whole dependency is skipped.

## Evidence

```js
const re = /#\s*renovate:\s*datasource=(?<datasource>\S+)\s+depName=(?<depName>\S+)\n[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*[:+?]?=\s*(?<currentValue>v?\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?\S*)/;
```
```
MATCH    "# renovate: datasource=go depName=github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser/v2"
NO MATCH "# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=golangci/golangci-lint versioning=semver"
NO MATCH "# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=kubernetes/kubernetes extractVersion=^v(?<version>.*)$"
```

## Impact

A consuming repo copies the comment form straight from Renovate's regex-manager documentation, which
routinely includes `versioning=`, and the tool version is never updated. Silent, and the failure looks
identical to "no update available".

The gap compounds with `versioningTemplate: "semver"` being hardcoded at `default.json:37`: a user who
tries to correct the versioning per-dependency via the comment gets a manager that ignores the comment
*and* refuses to match the line.

## Fix

Terminate the `depName` capture at end-of-line instead of at the newline, and allow trailing fields:

```
#\s*renovate:\s*datasource=(?<datasource>\S+)\s+depName=(?<depName>\S+)(?:\s+versioning=(?<versioning>\S+))?[^\n]*\n[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*[:+?]?=\s*(?<currentValue>v?\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?\S*)
```

Capturing `versioning` here also lets the hardcoded `versioningTemplate` be dropped.
Update `README.md:94` to match.

## Resolution
Match string now tolerates trailing comment fields in any order and captures versioning: depName=(?<depName>\S+)(?:[^\n]*?[ \t]versioning=(?<versioning>\S+))?[^\n]*\n. Verified against test/fixtures/Makefile that versioning=semver, versioning=node and extractVersion=... forms all extract.
title: Makefile manager silently skips the standard '# renovate: ... versioning=X' comment form

body:
## Problem

`default.json:35` accepts a two-part version — `(?<currentValue>v?\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?\S*)` makes the patch
segment optional — while `default.json:37` pins `"versioningTemplate": "semver"`. Renovate's `semver`
versioning is strict `x.y.z`; `1.21` is not a valid version under it. The manager therefore extracts a
dependency it cannot then resolve.

`README.md:99-100` states both halves in one sentence: *"the version may be two- or three-part (`1.21` or
`1.21.0`, optional leading `v`). Uses `semver` versioning."* Those two clauses contradict each other.

## Evidence

Renovate `lib/modules/versioning/semver/index.ts`:
```ts
export function isVersion(input: string): boolean {
  return !!valid(input);          // node-semver's semver.valid
}
export { getSatisfyingVersion, isVersion as isValid };
```
node-semver, run directly:
```
semver.valid("1.21")     = null
semver.valid("v1.21")    = null
semver.valid("1.21.0")   = "1.21.0"
semver.valid("v2.14.1")  = "2.14.1"
```
And the regex does match the two-part form, so the dep is extracted before it fails:
```
MATCH "# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=golang/go" -> currentValue=1.21
```

## Impact

Failing scenario: a Makefile carries the very common
```make
# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=golang/go
GO_VERSION := 1.21
```
Renovate extracts `currentValue: "1.21"`, `versioning: "semver"`, finds `isValid("1.21") === false`, and
skips the dependency. The user followed the documented pattern and gets no updates and no error.

## Fix

Drop the hardcoded template from `default.json` so each dependency uses its datasource's natural
versioning, or switch to one that tolerates partial versions:

```json
"versioningTemplate": "{{#if versioning}}{{{versioning}}}{{else}}semver-coerced{{/if}}"
```

(paired with capturing `versioning` from the comment — see the related Makefile match-string finding).
Then correct `README.md:99-100` to state the actual supported form.

## Resolution
versioningTemplate is now {{#if versioning}}{{{versioning}}}{{else}}semver-coerced{{/if}} — the comment's versioning wins when present, otherwise semver-coerced, which accepts two-part versions where strict semver returns null. test/check-managers.mjs asserts GO_VERSION := 1.21 extracts and fails outright if versioningTemplate is ever pinned back to 'semver'. README corrected.
title: versioningTemplate 'semver' rejects the two-part versions the regex accepts and the README documents

body:
## Problem

`default.json:203-217` sets `"groupName": "@ivuorinen packages"` for `@ivuorinen/**`. Later rules in the
same array set their own `groupName` using **unanchored** regexes:

- `default.json:270-274` — `"groupName": "eslint"`, `matchPackageNames: ["/eslint/"]`
- `default.json:289-294` — `"groupName": "semantic-release"`, `matchPackageNames: ["/semantic-release/"]`
- `default.json:295-300` — `"groupName": "stylelint"`, `matchPackageNames: ["/stylelint/"]`

Renovate applies `packageRules` in array order and later matches override earlier ones, so for any
`@ivuorinen` package whose name contains one of those substrings the `groupName` is replaced.

## Evidence

Renovate `docs/usage/configuration-options.md:3132-3134`:
> Order your `packageRules` so the least important rules are at the _top_, and the most important rules at
> the _bottom_. This way important rules override settings from earlier rules if needed.

Published packages in the scope (npm registry search for `@ivuorinen`, 2026-07-27) that match a later group:

| Package | Matched by | Resulting groupName |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@ivuorinen/eslint-config` | `/eslint/` | `eslint` |
| `@ivuorinen/stylelint-config` | `/stylelint/` | `stylelint` |
| `@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y` | `/stylelint/` | `stylelint` |
| `@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` | `/semantic-release/` | `semantic-release` |

That is 4 of the 12 packages published under the scope.

## Impact

Failing scenario: `@ivuorinen/eslint-config` publishes a fix. The fast-track rule's intent is a dedicated
`@ivuorinen packages` branch, created immediately, at any time, with no release-age hold. Instead the
upgrade is placed on the shared `eslint` branch alongside third-party eslint packages — while still
carrying `minimumReleaseAge: null`, `internalChecksFilter: "flexible"`, `schedule: ["at any time"]`,
`prPriority: 10` and `automerge: true` from the earlier rule. The fast-track path is broken for a third of
the scope, and the cooldown-bypass settings now sit on a branch shared with unaudited third-party packages.

## Fix

Move the `@ivuorinen packages` and `@ivuorinen actions` rules to the **end** of the `packageRules` array,
after the ecosystem groups — the position Renovate's docs prescribe for the rules that must win. No field
values need to change.

## Resolution
Moved both @ivuorinen rules to the end of packageRules (indices 26-27, after all ecosystem groups). @ivuorinen/eslint-config, stylelint-config, stylelint-a11y and semantic-release-config now keep the fast-track groupName. Added description blocks on the rules and notes in README and CLAUDE.md recording that the position is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
title: groupName collision drops 4 of 12 published @ivuorinen packages out of the fast-track group

body:
## Problem

The custom manager at `default.json:30-33` uses `managerFilePatterns: ["/(^|/)Makefile$/", "/\\.mk$/"]` —
slash-wrapped regex, matching `Makefile` at any depth. The group rule meant to collect its output
(`default.json:254-263`) uses `matchFileNames: ["Makefile", "**/*.mk"]`, where `"Makefile"` is a bare
minimatch glob that matches the exact path `Makefile` only.

## Evidence

Renovate `docs/usage/configuration-options.md:3115` and the worked example at 3119-3130:
> If you wish to limit Renovate to apply configuration rules to certain files in the root repository
> directory, you have to use `matchFileNames` with a `minimatch` glob (which can include an exact file
> name match) or RE2 regex.
>
> For example you have multiple `package.json` and want to use `dependencyDashboardApproval` only on the
> root `package.json`: `"matchFileNames": ["package.json"]`

The docs use exactly this construction to mean "root file only". Note the sibling entry `**/*.mk` is
written correctly; only the `Makefile` entry is inconsistent.

## Impact

Failing scenario: a repo keeps its tool versions in `build/Makefile`. The manager extracts the dependencies
(its pattern matches any directory), but the group rule does not apply, so each tool gets its own
ungrouped branch and PR instead of the single "development tools" PR the preset promises in
`README.md:133`. The inconsistency is invisible — nothing errors, the PRs just multiply.

## Fix

Make the group's glob match the manager's scope in `default.json:256-259`:

```json
"matchFileNames": ["**/Makefile", "**/*.mk"]
```

`**/Makefile` matches the root `Makefile` as well as any nested one.

## Resolution
matchFileNames changed from [Makefile, **/*.mk] to [**/Makefile, **/*.mk]. **/Makefile matches the root file as well as nested ones, so the group now covers the same scope the manager collects. README table updated.
title: 'development tools' group matches only the repo-root Makefile while the manager collects Makefiles in any directory

body:
## Problem

`.github/renovate.json:10-20` declares:
```json
{
  "automerge": true,
  "matchPackageNames": ["renovate", "renovate/renovate", "renovatebot/**"],
  "separateMinorPatch": false
}
```
There is no `matchUpdateTypes`, so the rule applies to **major** updates as well. The only dependency it
actually matches in this repo is `renovatebot/pre-commit-hooks` — the hook that runs
`renovate-config-validator`, i.e. the repo's sole correctness check on `default.json`.

## Evidence

`.pre-commit-config.yaml:18-27` pins `renovatebot/pre-commit-hooks` at `rev: 43.252.1` and is the only
consumer of that repo. Git history shows the rule working as intended for minor bumps (`494cf33`, `c712eff`,
`ae9e213`). Nothing in the config restricts it to non-major.

Combined with the absence of any CI workflow (see the CI-gate finding), a major bump merges with no
validator run at all — the validator being the thing that just changed.

## Impact

Failing scenario: `renovatebot/pre-commit-hooks` ships a major release that renames or removes the
`renovate-config-validator` hook id. Renovate raises `chore(deps)!: update ...`, automerges it, and `main`
now carries a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` referencing a hook that no longer exists. Every subsequent
`prek run` fails at hook resolution, and the preset is left unvalidated until someone notices manually.

## Fix

Scope the automerge to non-breaking updates in `.github/renovate.json`:

```json
{
  "automerge": true,
  "matchPackageNames": ["renovate", "renovate/renovate", "renovatebot/**"],
  "matchUpdateTypes": ["minor", "patch"],
  "separateMinorPatch": false
}
```
Major bumps then raise a reviewable PR.

## Resolution
Added matchUpdateTypes:[minor,patch] to the renovatebot self-update rule in .github/renovate.json; majors now raise a reviewable PR. Required splitting the rule in two — Renovate rejects combining matchUpdateTypes with separateMinorPatch (caught by renovate-config-validator during the fix), so separateMinorPatch:false stays in its own rule without matchUpdateTypes.
title: This repo automerges major updates of its own validator hook, with no CI gate behind it

area: repository root (no test fixtures for customManagers)
body:
## Problem

`default.json` ships two `customManagers` whose entire value is in regex behaviour, and the repository has
no fixture exercising either. `renovate-config-validator --strict` checks that a match string *compiles*;
it never checks that it *matches* anything. `check-jsonschema` validates JSON shape only.

## Evidence

```
$ git ls-files
.editorconfig
.github/renovate.json
.gitignore
.pre-commit-config.yaml
CLAUDE.md
LICENSE
README.md
default.json
```
No fixture Dockerfile, no fixture Makefile, no test directory. `CLAUDE.md` states plainly: *"No build
system, no tests, no application code."*

All three validators pass on the current tree:
```
renovate-config-validator................................................Passed
renovate-config-validator (repo config)..................................Passed
check-renovate-preset....................................................Passed
```
yet this audit found three separate extraction defects in those same regexes — `[A-Z]+_VERSION` missing
multi-word names, `depName=(\S+)\n` breaking on the documented `versioning=` suffix, and
`versioningTemplate: "semver"` rejecting the two-part versions the regex accepts. Each is caught by a
one-line fixture. The green hook run is what makes this a coverage hole rather than a preference.

## Impact

Every future edit to these match strings ships unverified. The failure mode is silent — Renovate extracts
nothing and reports nothing — so a regression is only noticed when someone asks why a tool stopped
updating, potentially months later.

## Fix

Add `test/fixtures/Dockerfile` and `test/fixtures/Makefile` covering the documented forms, plus a
`renovate --platform=local --dry-run=extract` check driven from the CI workflow the CI-gate finding calls
for. A minimal version needs no framework:

```sh
npx --yes renovate --platform=local --dry-run=extract 2>&1 \
  | grep -q 'DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION' || { echo 'Dockerfile ENV manager regressed'; exit 1; }
```

Note `test/**` and `tests/**` are in `ignorePaths` (`default.json:69-71`), so fixtures there will not be
picked up by consumers' Renovate runs — keep them under `test/fixtures/` deliberately.

## Resolution
Added test/fixtures/{Dockerfile,Makefile} and test/check-managers.mjs, which reads the matchStrings out of default.json (so it cannot drift from the config) and asserts what they extract. Wired as a local pre-commit hook 'check-custom-managers', so it runs locally and in the new CI workflow. Verified non-tautological: replaying the pre-fix regexes against it fails 4 of 6 checks and exits 1.
title: The two custom regex managers have no fixtures, which is why three extraction defects shipped undetected

body:
## Problem

`.github/renovate.json:6` sets a top-level `"automergeType": "pr"`, reading as a deliberate choice to keep
this repo on PR-based automerge. It has no effect. `packageRules` override top-level config, and
`default.json:89-97` sets `"automergeType": "branch"` for `minor`, `patch` and `digest` — the only update
types this repo ever automerges (major updates carry no `automerge: true`).

The value is also the Renovate default (`lib/config/options/index.ts`), so it does nothing even where it is
not overridden.

## Evidence

Renovate `docs/usage/configuration-options.md:3132-3134` — `packageRules` are applied after and override
top-level settings. The preset's rule sets `automergeType` unconditionally for the three automerged types,
and nothing in `.github/renovate.json` re-asserts it at rule level.

## Impact

Misleading rather than harmful: a reader of `.github/renovate.json` concludes this repo's dependency
updates arrive as reviewable pull requests, when in fact minor/patch/digest updates are branch-automerged
straight to `main` with no PR. That mismatch matters here because this repo has no CI gate.

## Fix

Either delete the inert line, or make the intent effective by moving it into a rule:

```json
{ "automergeType": "pr", "matchUpdateTypes": ["minor", "patch", "digest"] }
```

## Resolution
Removed the inert top-level automergeType from .github/renovate.json and replaced it with a packageRule {automergeType: pr, matchUpdateTypes: [minor, patch]}, which actually overrides the preset's per-updateType rule. Description records why a top-level value cannot work here.
title: automergeType 'pr' in the repo config is inert — the preset's packageRule overrides it for every automerged update type

body:
## Problem

`README.md:183` lists the validation hooks as **`check-renovate`**, and `CLAUDE.md` repeats it: *"and
`check-renovate` (JSON Schema validation via check-jsonschema)"*. The hook is named
`check-renovate-preset` in `.pre-commit-config.yaml:31`.

## Evidence

`.pre-commit-config.yaml:29-38`:
```yaml
  - repo: https://github.com/python-jsonschema/check-jsonschema
    rev: 0.37.4
    hooks:
      - id: check-jsonschema
        name: check-renovate-preset
```
Actual run output:
```
check-renovate-preset....................................................Passed
```

## Impact

`prek run check-renovate` and `pre-commit run check-renovate` both fail with "no hook with id
`check-renovate`" — the documented command for running just the schema check does not work.

## Fix

Replace `check-renovate` with `check-renovate-preset` in `README.md:183` and in the Validation section of
`CLAUDE.md`.

## Resolution
README and CLAUDE.md now name the hook check-renovate-preset. Both files also gained the new check-custom-managers hook and a note that renovate-config-validator now runs against both JSON files.
title: Docs name the schema hook 'check-renovate'; the configured hook is 'check-renovate-preset'

## Problem

`CLAUDE.md` states: *"Sets `postUpdateOptions` for lock file deduplication across bundler, composer, go,
npm, pnpm, and yarn."* Two of the six configured options are not deduplication.

## Evidence

`default.json:314-321`:
```json
"postUpdateOptions": [
  "bundlerConservative",     <- conservative resolution, not dedupe
  "composerWithAll",         <- composer update --with-all-dependencies, not dedupe
  "gomodUpdateImportPaths",  <- rewrites import paths on major bumps, not dedupe
  "npmDedupe",
  "pnpmDedupe",
  "yarnDedupeHighest"
]
```
`README.md:150-157` describes each option correctly; only `CLAUDE.md` generalises them all as
deduplication.

## Impact

`CLAUDE.md` is the file an agent reads before editing this repo. The summary implies the six options are
interchangeable members of one category, which invites dropping or swapping one — e.g. removing
`gomodUpdateImportPaths` as "redundant with npmDedupe" — and breaks Go major updates.

## Fix

Reword to match `README.md`: *"Sets `postUpdateOptions` for post-update lock file handling: dedupe for npm,
pnpm and yarn; conservative resolution for bundler; `--with-all-dependencies` for composer; import-path
rewriting for go."*

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md now describes each postUpdateOptions entry by what it does (dedupe for npm/pnpm/yarn, conservative resolution for bundler, --with-all-dependencies for composer, import-path rewriting for go) and warns against dropping one as redundant.
title: CLAUDE.md describes postUpdateOptions as lock-file deduplication; half the listed options do something else

body:
## Problem

`renovate-config-validator` treats any explicitly-passed filename as a **global self-hosted** config
unless `--no-global` is given. Both hooks in `.pre-commit-config.yaml:18-27` pass a filename and neither
passes `--no-global`, so `default.json` (a shared preset) and `.github/renovate.json` (a repository config)
are both validated against the global schema — a superset that permits every `globalOnly` option.

The repository-vs-global distinction is the whole point of the check. A `globalOnly` option placed in a
shared preset is silently ignored by every consumer, and this validator, as wired, will not say so.

## Evidence

Renovate `lib/config-validator.ts:140` (CLI help):
> When specifying [config-files...], Renovate will treat them as global self-hosted configuration files.
> You can disable this behaviour with `--no-global`

The hooks' own output confirms the mode:
```
$ prek run --all-files
renovate-config-validator (repo config)..................................Passed
  INFO: Validating .github/renovate.json as global config
```

Reintroducing `onboardingConfigFileName` into `default.json` — the exact `globalOnly` option a previous
audit found and removed — is accepted under the current arguments:
```
$ renovate-config-validator --strict <default.json + onboardingConfigFileName>
 INFO: Validating ... as global config
 INFO: Config validated successfully against 1 file(s)
exit=0

$ renovate-config-validator --strict --no-global <same file>
 INFO: Validating ... as repo config
 WARN: Found errors in configuration
       "message": "The \"onboardingConfigFileName\" option is a global option reserved only for
                   Renovate's global configuration and cannot be configured within a repository's
                   config file."
exit=1
```

## Impact

Failing scenario: someone adds `onboardingConfigFileName`, `binarySource`, `dockerUser`, `allowedCommands`
or any other `globalOnly` option to `default.json`. Every hook passes, CI passes, the commit lands on
`main`, and every repository extending the preset silently ignores the option — or raises a config-error
issue at runtime. This is precisely the defect class a prior audit had to find by hand, and the gate that
was supposed to prevent a recurrence does not fire.

The impact grew with the new CI workflow: this is now the gate on every push and pull request, so the
wrong mode is baked into the pipeline rather than just a local convenience.

## Fix

Add `--no-global` to both validator hooks in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
      - id: renovate-config-validator
        files: default.json
        args: [--strict, --no-global]
      - id: renovate-config-validator
        name: renovate-config-validator (repo config)
        files: .github/renovate.json
        args: [--strict, --no-global]
```

Confirm the mode flipped by checking the hook output reads `as repo config`, not `as global config`.

## Resolution
Added --no-global to both renovate-config-validator hooks. Hook output now reads 'Validating default.json as repo config' and 'Validating .github/renovate.json as repo config'. Verified the gate works: default.json plus onboardingConfigFileName exits 0 in global mode and 1 in repo mode. Comment in .pre-commit-config.yaml records why the flag is required.
title: Both validator hooks run in global-config mode, so globalOnly options in a repo config or shared preset pass silently

body:
## Problem

`test/check-managers.mjs` exists because `renovate-config-validator` proves a regex compiles but never that it matches. The commit-message surface has the identical gap and no equivalent guard: the validator accepts any string in `commitMessagePrefix`, so a prefix that is not a valid conventional commit, or that reintroduces the `!` breaking marker on GitHub Actions, ships green through every hook and every CI run.

## Evidence

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs four checks against `default.json`: `pretty-format-json`, `renovate-config-validator --strict --no-global`, `check-jsonschema` against `renovate-schema.json`, and `check-managers`. None inspects `commitMessagePrefix`.

Renovate's schema types `commitMessagePrefix` as a plain string, so all of these validate clean today:

```json
{ "commitMessagePrefix": "Chore(Deps): " }      // subject-case / type-case failure
{ "commitMessagePrefix": "chore(deps)!: ", "matchManagers": ["github-actions"] }
{ "commitMessagePrefix": "deps: " }             // type not in commitlint's type-enum
```

The second is precisely the state the repository was in before the never-breaking rule was added, and precisely the state a careless reorder of `packageRules` restores — the new rule only wins because it sits after the global major rule, and nothing asserts that ordering. The comment in the rule's `description` is the sole protection, and comments do not fail builds.

## Impact

A regression in the commit-prefix shape is undetectable until it reaches a consuming repository, where it either fails commitlint or, in the `!` case, silently cuts a major release across every repo that extends the preset. Because consumers extend `github>ivuorinen/renovate-config` at default-branch HEAD, the blast radius is immediate and repo-wide.

## Fix

Add `test/check-commit-messages.mjs`, mirroring `check-managers.mjs`: read `default.json`, walk `packageRules`, and assert

1. every `commitMessagePrefix` matches `/^[a-z]+(\([a-z][a-z-]*\))?!?: $/` with the type drawn from commitlint's `type-enum` (`build|chore|ci|docs|feat|fix|perf|refactor|revert|style|test`);
2. no rule whose `matchManagers` includes `github-actions` carries a `!` in its prefix;
3. for every rule that both matches `github-actions` and sets a prefix, its index is greater than the index of every rule setting a `!` prefix that could also match it — the ordering invariant the design depends on.

Register it in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` next to `check-managers`, same `language: system` / `node` entry, so it runs locally and in CI. Zero new dependencies: the assertions are string checks, not a commitlint invocation.

## Resolution
Added test/check-commit-messages.mjs and registered it as a check-commit-messages hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml, so it runs locally and in CI. It asserts all three invariants: valid conventional-commit prefix (type drawn from commitlint's type-enum, lower-case scope), no breaking marker on any github-actions-scoped rule, and the actions override sitting after every unscoped breaking prefix. Zero new dependencies. Verified by mutation: a "!" restored on actions, an invalid type, an upper-case type/scope, the override moved to the front of packageRules, and the override deleted outright each exit 1; the unmutated config exits 0. Documented in CLAUDE.md and the README Validation section.</notes>
</invoke>
title: No check guards the commit-message shape the preset emits

body:
## Problem

The sign-off is configured as `"commitBody": "Signed-off-by: {{{gitAuthor}}}"`. Renovate's documentation for `commitBody` directs the opposite: git trailers belong in `commitTrailers`, and the built-in `:gitSignOff` preset is the supported way to sign off. `commitBody` is a plain string and therefore non-mergeable, so any consuming repo that sets its own `commitBody` overwrites this one and drops the DCO sign-off from every commit — with no error and no validator complaint. `commitTrailers` is an array marked `mergeable: true`, so a consumer adding a trailer keeps the sign-off.

## Evidence

Renovate configuration-options docs, `commitBody`:
> To add git trailers like `Signed-off-by` to commits, use `commitTrailers` instead.

Renovate configuration-options docs, `commitTrailers` (`type: array`, `mergeable: true`):
> If you want Renovate to sign off its commits, you can add the `:gitSignOff` preset to your `extends` array.

Renovate default-presets docs, `:gitSignOff`:
```json
{ "commitTrailers": ["Signed-off-by: {{{gitAuthor}}}"] }
```

Failing scenario: a consuming repo follows the `commitBody` example in Renovate's own docs — `{"commitBody": "[skip ci]"}` — to keep dependency bumps out of CI. Because `commitBody` is a single non-mergeable string and the consumer's config is applied after the preset, every Renovate commit in that repo now carries `[skip ci]` and no `Signed-off-by:` line. A repository with DCO enforcement then rejects the push, or accepts unsigned commits, depending on which check runs.

This supersedes the "not a bug — just non-DRY" assessment in NIT-017: the two forms differ in merge behavior and in trailer-block placement, not only in spelling.

## Impact

Silent loss of the DCO sign-off in any consuming repo that sets `commitBody`. Additionally, if this preset ever gains a real `commitBody`, the sign-off would sit in the message body rather than the trailer block, where `git interpret-trailers` and DCO bots look for it.

## Fix

In `default.json`, delete the `"commitBody"` key and add `":gitSignOff"` to `extends` (alphabetically after `:enableVulnerabilityAlerts`). The rendered commit text is byte-identical when no other body is set — subject, blank line, `Signed-off-by:` — so no commit-message shape changes and commitlint's verdict is unaffected. Update the README "Key settings" row and the "Extends" table accordingly.

## Resolution
Removed the literal commitBody from default.json and added ":gitSignOff" to extends, which sets commitTrailers: ["Signed-off-by: {{{gitAuthor}}}"] — the form Renovate's docs direct git trailers to, and mergeable, so a consuming repo adding its own commitBody or trailer no longer drops the DCO sign-off. Rendered commit text is unchanged when no other body is set, so no commit-message shape changed. renovate-config-validator --strict --no-global and check-renovate-preset both pass. README Extends and Key settings tables updated; CLAUDE.md records why the preset is used instead of the literal.</notes>
</invoke>
title: DCO sign-off uses commitBody, which a consumer's own commitBody silently replaces

body:
## Problem

Both `@ivuorinen` fast-track rules set `automerge: true` with `minimumReleaseAge: null`, `schedule: ["at any time"]`, `prCreation: "immediate"` and no `matchUpdateTypes` restriction. Every update type — major included — is therefore merged unattended, immediately, with the 3-day cooldown that protects every other dependency explicitly switched off.

## Evidence

`default.json`, `@ivuorinen packages` rule: `"automerge": true`, `"automergeType": "pr"`, `"minimumReleaseAge": null`, `"schedule": ["at any time"]`, `"prCreation": "immediate"`, `"matchPackageNames": ["@ivuorinen/**"]`. No `matchUpdateTypes`, so the rule applies to majors as well. The `@ivuorinen actions` rule is identical in shape for `ivuorinen/actions*`.

By contrast this repo's own `.github/renovate.json` restricts its self-update automerge to minor and patch, with the reason recorded in the rule: "a major bump can rename or drop the hook id. Majors get a review." The preset does not apply that reasoning to its own first-party packages.

Failing scenario: an npm token for the `@ivuorinen` scope is compromised and a malicious `@ivuorinen/eslint-config` is published. `minimumReleaseAge: null` removes the 3-day window in which npm unpublishes and malware scanners act; `schedule: ["at any time"]` removes the non-office-hours gate; `automerge: true` merges it into every repo extending this preset on Renovate's next run. The `minimumReleaseAge: "3 days"` hold that the config describes as protecting against exactly this is bypassed for the one scope whose compromise affects every repository at once.

## Impact

A first-party account or token compromise propagates to every consuming repository within one Renovate cycle, with no cooldown and no human in the loop. The exposure is bounded by control of the `@ivuorinen` npm scope and the `ivuorinen/actions` repository, which is why this is Low rather than higher — but it is the single largest unattended-merge surface in the preset, and majors are included in it.

## Fix

If the fast-track is deliberate for minors and patches only — matching the reasoning already written into `.github/renovate.json` — add `"matchUpdateTypes": ["minor", "patch"]` to both `@ivuorinen` rules, leaving majors to raise a reviewable PR. Note that the rules must keep their `groupName` applying to all update types to preserve the ordering fix recorded in their `description`, so add a second rule rather than narrowing the existing one if the group must stay universal.

If unattended major automerge is intentional, extend the rules' `description` blocks to say so and to name the accepted risk, and close this finding as accepted — the code already reads as if no one considered majors.

## Resolution
Split each @ivuorinen fast-track into two rules: a grouping rule keeping groupName, prPriority, prCreation, schedule and minimumReleaseAge: null for every update type (so the ordering fix that stops the ecosystem regexes overwriting groupName is preserved), and a separate automerge rule restricted to minor/patch for @ivuorinen packages and minor/patch/digest for @ivuorinen actions. Digest is retained for ivuorinen/actions specifically because that rule is the one trusted digest source; third-party action digests still raise a reviewable PR. First-party majors now get an immediate top-priority PR instead of an unattended merge, matching the reasoning already written into .github/renovate.json for renovatebot/**. README gained a "First-party majors are not automerged" section; CLAUDE.md records the split.</notes>
</invoke>
title: First-party packages automerge majors with no release-age hold and no schedule gate

body:
## Problem

The README describes the generated commit prefix in three places and each is wrong in a different way. It claims `:semanticCommits` yields `chore(deps):`, omitting the `fix(deps):` half that `config:recommended` produces for runtime dependencies. It states GitHub Actions major bumps use `chore(deps)!:`, which the new never-breaking rule has just made false. And it presents the major rule's `chore(deps)!:` prefix as the outcome for all majors without noting that the literal prefix defeats the `fix`/`chore` split for every major update.

## Evidence

`config:recommended` pulls in `:semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers`, which sets `semanticCommitType: "fix"` for `dependencies`/`require` dep types and `chore` for everything else. Runtime dependency updates therefore commit as `fix(deps): update dependency foo (1.0.0 → 1.1.0)`.

- `README.md:32` — `:semanticCommits` | "Use conventional commit messages (`chore(deps):`)". Only half the truth.
- `README.md:154` — the `github-actions` row reads "scope: `actions` (non-major; major bumps use `chore(deps)!:`)". After the never-breaking rule, actions majors commit as `chore(actions):`, with no `!` at all.
- `README.md:139` — "Major commit prefix | `matchUpdateTypes: ["major"]` | `chore(deps)!:` prefix". True as written, but the rule sets `commitMessagePrefix` literally, which overrides the semantic prefix wholesale, so a runtime-dependency major commits as `chore(deps)!:` rather than the `fix(deps)!:` the split would otherwise give. The README does not say so.

This is the still-open NIT-018 ("Minor doc imprecision", advisory) plus a new contradiction introduced by the actions rule. The README is the only place a consuming repo learns what its release automation will see, so a wrong prefix table is a wrong release plan.

## Impact

A consumer reading the README sets up semantic-release or a changelog config expecting `chore(deps):` only, and is surprised by a patch release from every runtime dependency bump. A reader of README:154 believes actions majors still carry the breaking marker, which is the exact opposite of the design choice just recorded in CLAUDE.md.

## Fix

In `README.md`:
- line 32 — change the `:semanticCommits` description to "Conventional commit messages: `fix(deps):` for runtime dependencies (via `:semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers` in `config:recommended`), `chore(deps):` for everything else".
- line 139 — append to the major row: "the literal prefix overrides the `fix`/`chore` split, so runtime-dependency majors also commit as `chore(deps)!:`".
- line 154 — replace "(non-major; major bumps use `chore(deps)!:`)" with "`chore(actions):` for every update type — actions majors are deliberately never marked breaking".
- add a row for the new never-breaking rule to the "Automerge and labeling" table.

Then resolve NIT-018, which this supersedes.

## Resolution
All three README sites corrected. The :semanticCommits row now states the fix(deps)/chore(deps) split that :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers produces. The major-prefix row notes that the literal commitMessagePrefix overrides the semantic prefix wholesale, so runtime-dependency majors also commit as chore(deps)!:. The github-actions row no longer claims majors use chore(deps)!: — it now reads "scope: actions, for every update type — actions bumps are never marked breaking". Added a dedicated "Actions are never breaking" row to the Automerge and labeling table naming the ordering requirement and the check that enforces it.</notes>
</invoke>
title: README documents commit prefixes that the config does not generate

body:
## Problem

The `@ivuorinen packages` rule sets `"internalChecksFilter": "flexible"` and, in the same object, `"minimumReleaseAge": null`. Renovate's documentation states that `internalChecksFilter` "applies to the `minimumReleaseAge` check only". With no minimum release age in force for the matched packages there is no pending-release check to filter, so the option does nothing.

## Evidence

Renovate configuration-options docs, `internalChecksFilter`:
> This setting determines whether Renovate controls when and how filtering of internal checks are performed, particularly when multiple versions of the same update type are available. Currently this applies to the `minimumReleaseAge` check only.

The rule is last in `packageRules`, so its `minimumReleaseAge: null` wins over both the top-level `minimumReleaseAge: "3 days"` and the `security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm` preset rule — which is exactly what the README documents for this group ("no release-age hold").

The sibling `@ivuorinen actions` rule sets `minimumReleaseAge: null` and omits `internalChecksFilter`, and behaves identically. The asymmetry is the tell: the option is left over from before the rules were moved to the end of the array, when `minimumReleaseAge: null` did not yet win.

## Impact

No behavior change; the cost is that a reader must check `internalChecksFilter`'s semantics against a second key in the same object to learn it is dead, and a future edit that reintroduces a release-age hold for `@ivuorinen/*` would silently switch on "flexible" PR flapping that nobody chose — the mode Renovate's own docs recommend against.

## Fix

Remove the `"internalChecksFilter": "flexible"` line from the `@ivuorinen packages` rule in `default.json`, leaving the two fast-track rules symmetric. Drop it from the README "Dependency groups" row if listed there.

## Resolution
Removed "internalChecksFilter": "flexible" from the @ivuorinen packages rule. With minimumReleaseAge: null in the same rule there was no pending-release check for it to filter, and the sibling @ivuorinen actions rule already omitted it. The two fast-tracks are now symmetric. Hooks pass.</notes>
</invoke>
title: internalChecksFilter on the @ivuorinen packages rule is inert

body:
## Problem

`validate.yml` pins both actions to full SHA digests and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` pins every hook repo by `rev`, but the workflow installs the tool that executes all of them with a bare `pip install pre-commit`. The one unpinned input is the one with the most privilege in the job.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/validate.yml`:
```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: pip install pre-commit
      - run: pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
```
`pip install pre-commit` resolves the latest release, plus its full transitive tree, at job time. Neither `python-version: '3.x'` nor the install is constrained, so two runs of the same commit can execute different code. Renovate cannot see the dependency either: no manager extracts a bare `pip install` in a `run:` step, so it is invisible to the same update pipeline this repository exists to configure.

Consequence in practice: a broken `pre-commit` release turns CI red on an unchanged commit, and the failure surfaces as a hook error rather than an install problem.

## Impact

Non-reproducible CI, and an unpinned execution path in the job that gates the only artifact consumers read. The workflow has `permissions: contents: read` and no secrets, so the compromise ceiling is a false-green validation rather than repository write — which is why this is Low.

## Fix

Pin the install and make it Renovate-visible:
```yaml
      - run: pip install pre-commit==4.5.0 # renovate: datasource=pypi depName=pre-commit
```
The trailing comment is not picked up by any manager here; to have Renovate track it, either move the pin into a `requirements.txt` (covered by the built-in `pip_requirements` manager) or add a `pypi` custom manager for `pip install <pkg>==<version>` lines in workflow files. Pin `python-version` to a concrete minor (`'3.13'`) in the same change.

## Resolution
Pinned via a new .github/workflows/requirements.txt containing pre-commit==4.6.2, with the workflow now running "pip install -r .github/workflows/requirements.txt". A requirements.txt was chosen over an inline ==pin so Renovate's built-in pip_requirements manager tracks the upgrade — a bare pip install in a run: step is invisible to every manager. python-version also pinned from '3.x' to '3.13'. The whole job is now pinned end to end: both actions by SHA, every hook repo by rev, and the tool that executes them by version.</notes>
</invoke>
title: CI installs pre-commit unpinned while every other input is pinned

body:
## Problem

`commitMessageExtra` is overridden to ` ({{currentVersion}} → {{newVersion}})`, replacing Renovate's default `to v1.2.3`. The custom form spends roughly 20 extra characters on every header. For dependencies with long names — Docker images with a full registry path are the common case — the resulting header exceeds the `header-max-length` of 100 that `@commitlint/config-conventional` enforces at error level, so the commit fails `commitlint` in every consuming repo that runs it.

## Evidence

Nineteen headers this preset can generate were linted with commitlint 21.2.2 against ivuorinen/base-configs-commitlint (`extends: ["@commitlint/config-conventional"]`, `rules: {"body-leading-blank": [2, "always"]}`). Two failed, both on length:

```
FAIL [hdr=103] chore(deps): update image mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet (8.0.10-bookworm-slim → 8.0.11-bookworm-slim)
       ERROR  header-max-length: header must not be longer than 100 characters, current length is 103
FAIL [hdr=111] chore(deps): update image mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet (8.0.10-bookworm-slim → 8.0.11-bookworm-slim) (#1234)
       ERROR  header-max-length: header must not be longer than 100 characters, current length is 111
```

The same update under Renovate's default `commitMessageExtra` is `chore(deps): update image mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet to v8.0.11-bookworm-slim` — 81 characters, passing. The override is the sole cause.

This repo's own history is already at 94 of the 100 characters (`chore(deps): update pre-commit hook python-jsonschema/check-jsonschema (0.37.4 → 0.38.0) (#59)`), so the remaining headroom is six characters. GitHub's squash merge appends ` (#N)`, which consumes five or six of them.

Renovate has no header-truncation option, so nothing in the preset caps the length.

## Impact

A Docker or long-path dependency update lands a red `commitlint` run. Where the preset automerges via `automergeType: "branch"` (all minor and patch updates), the failing commit is pushed straight to the default branch with no PR, so the consuming repo's default branch goes red and stays red until a human intervenes. Where the update raises a PR, the failing lint check blocks the merge and the update stalls silently.

## Fix

Two mutually exclusive options; the first keeps the version range that motivated the override.

1. Raise the limit on the commitlint side — in `ivuorinen/base-configs-commitlint/index.cjs`, add `"header-max-length": [2, "always", 120]` alongside the existing `body-leading-blank` rule. 120 clears the worst realistic case (111) with headroom. This is a change in a different repository and cannot be applied from here.
2. Drop the override — delete `commitMessageExtra` from `default.json` and accept Renovate's default `to v1.2.3`, losing the old-version half of the range.

Whichever is chosen, record it in `CLAUDE.md` next to the other commit-message design choices, and add the regression guard described in the `tests` finding on commit-prefix shape so the limit is checked in CI rather than rediscovered.

## Resolution
Resolved as a recorded acceptance, not a repair — the overflow still exists and is deliberate. User's decision: keep the (old → new) version range, accept that headers for long-registry-path Docker images exceed commitlint's header-max-length of 100 (measured 103, and 111 once GitHub's squash merge appends the PR ref). CLAUDE.md now carries the design choice with the measurement, the two rejected alternatives (drop commitMessageExtra, or raise the limit in ivuorinen/base-configs-commitlint), and the note that Renovate has no header-truncation option. Every other generated shape was verified clean against real commitlint 21.2.2: 17 of 19 reconstructed headers pass, the 2 failures are this case only.</notes>
</invoke>
title: commitMessageExtra pushes long-dependency headers past commitlint's 100-char limit
